# Reviewer Roles

The work changes meaningfully depending on which seat you're in. Identify the role at intake.

## Detailed Assessor (ARC; equivalent: ERC remote referee, SNSF external referee)

- Reads one or a few applications in depth.
- Scores against each criterion + writes detailed comments (ARC: min 500 chars/criterion, 3500 overall).
- Comments go to General Assessors / SAC AND to applicants at rejoinder stage.
- Should _not_ compare applications — assess on its own merits.
- Should _not_ restate the application or use generic comments.

**Implication for the workflow**: full evidence-cited comments per criterion. Long-form. Score and comment must align so applicants can use them in rejoinder.

## General Assessor / College of Experts (ARC SAC member; equivalent: ERC panel member, SNSF panel)

- Sits on the Selection Advisory Committee.
- Considers a broader pool — typically dozens — under finite time.
- _Uses_ Detailed Assessor scores and comments as inputs, alongside their own expertise and broad disciplinary judgment.
- Moderates across the pool, ranks within the panel's allocation, recommends funding.
- May be required to write briefer panel-facing notes rather than applicant-facing detailed assessments.

**Implication for the workflow**:

- Step 5 looks different — _triangulate_ across (a) the application itself, (b) Detailed Assessor scores/comments if visible in RMS, (c) your own disciplinary read.
- Reading notes should still cite the application, but the eventual product is panel-oriented (rank within pool, defend recommendation in committee), not 500-char-per-criterion applicant-facing prose.
- ROPE-on-opportunity and unconscious-bias checks still apply — arguably more important here because of cognitive load across many applications.
- The role is _moderation_, not de-novo detailed review. Don't ignore Detailed Assessor signals; don't be captured by them either.

## Collegial draft reviewer

- A colleague hands the user a paper, thesis, draft chapter, or grant draft for feedback before submission.
- The user provides the judgment; the agent supports.
- Use Scribe Mode in SKILL.md.

## Journal peer review

- Pre-publication review of a manuscript.
- Tone is more skeptical than for grants — focus on validity, rigor, what the data can/cannot support.
- Recommendation (accept/minor/major/reject) is a separate axis from criticism.

---

## Cross-role rules (always apply)

- **CoI declared once, carried as a flag.** Scan for conflicts at intake, declare, and carry the result as a one-line header flag on the review — don't re-litigate it every turn. The single residual that must recur is "confirm against your own records": the scan can't see private collaboration history, so the academic confirms that personally before submitting.
- No personal attacks.
- No integrity allegations in assessment text — route separately.
- No AI-generated assessment text under ARC policy (and verify equivalent policies for other schemes).
- Slow down to manage unconscious bias: halo, horns, confirmation, conformity, affinity, anchor.
